tier_rationale: A video baby monitor's core function is showing you the baby. Nanit's own product page states the monitor is viewed 'via your Nanit App and an Internet connection' with no local-network-only viewing path described anywhere, and repeated checks of Nanit's support site and third-party sources within budget found no documented way to view video without the cloud. Core function requires the cloud with no cited liberation path.
rejection_reason: Live video, the entire purpose of the device, is routed through Nanit's app and servers with no local-only viewing mode documented by the vendor. Basic live streaming and motion/sound notifications are free (no Insights subscription required), but the internet dependency itself is not optional — the vendor's own language ties viewing to 'an Internet connection,' not to a home network.
the_unplug_test: The camera stops showing you your baby. Live view, notifications, and two-way audio all route through the Nanit app and Nanit's servers, and the vendor's own product description ties viewing to having an internet connection, not merely a home network — there is no documented local/LAN-only fallback. The paid Insights plan governs sleep analytics and smart-speaker integration, not basic viewing, so cost is not the issue here; connectivity is.

sources.supports: Manufacturer's own product page: video is viewed 'via your Nanit App and an Internet connection'; live stream, motion/sound notifications, and two-way audio are free without a subscription; the paid Insights plan covers sleep analytics and Alexa/Google Home integration, not basic viewing; no local-network-only viewing mode is described. Price observed at $289.99 (sale) against a higher list price.
FCC grants 2AIWVN302 and 2AIWVN301 (grantee Udisense Inc. DBA Nanit) confirm dual-band 2.4/5 GHz WiFi radios in the Nanit Pro camera.

open_questions: Three attempts to reach Nanit's own support site (support.nanit.com and nanit.com/pages/faq) for an explicit 'does Nanit work without internet' statement returned 404s to automated fetch; a human check of that page would strengthen this record.
No documented, maintained third-party local-access path (ESPHome, Home Assistant community project, RTSP extraction) was found within budget. If one exists this should become a D3 record instead.
Exact current list price (pre-sale) not confirmed; $289.99 was an active discounted price at time of check.
notes: Direct contrast case for this domain: the Infant Optics DXR-8 PRO (also in this catalog) is a video baby monitor solving the same problem with a closed point-to-point link and no cloud at all. This record is not a claim that Nanit's video quality or features are bad — only that the core capability requires an internet connection to Nanit's servers by the vendor's own description, with no opt-out.
local_replacement_note: No documented local-only viewing path. Video is described by the vendor as requiring an internet connection rather than merely a home network.

alternatives.why: A video baby monitor that solves the same core problem (seeing the baby) over a closed point-to-point link with no app, no account, and no vendor cloud at any point. The tradeoff is no remote/away-from-home viewing, which Nanit offers and this does not.
Not a video alternative, but the DECT audio monitor already in this catalog for readers who decide audio-only local monitoring is an acceptable tradeoff for removing the cloud entirely.
